source.title: Decoupling Dynamical Richness from Representation Learning: Towards Practical Measurement
source.authors: Yoonsoo Nam; Nayara Fonseca; S. Lee; Chris Mingard; N. Göring; Ouns El Harzli; Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk; Soufiane Hayou; Ard A. Louis

record.tranche_reason: The study reports train and test accuracy at checkpoints before and after grokking on a modular arithmetic task, using its own richness measure and visualization rather than replicating the original study’s full method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a 2-layer transformer on mod-p division at steps 200 and 3000, explicitly identifying these as before and after grokking. Its DLR measurements at those checkpoints are recorded as related richness findings, not as evidence for the more specific circuit-formation claim in V2. Other reported comparisons, including image-task training-factor experiments, do not measure delayed generalization as described by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses grokking as a known lazy-to-rich transition to check that its DLR metric behaves as expected. It reproduces grokking on mod-97 division with a 2-layer transformer (teddykoker code) and reports only two hand-picked checkpoints (steps 200 and 3000) to show DLR falls. It draws no conclusion about grokking itself. It does not measure the delay, vary training-set size, or probe mechanism. The accuracy numbers are illustrative setup values for validating the metric, not a test of V1. The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 'supports' label are therefore withdrawn.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors propose DLR as a cheap, performance-independent richness metric that recovers neural collapse as a special case. They say it captures known lazy-to-rich transitions such as grokking and target downscaling, and they stress that rich dynamics do not imply better generalization. Grokking serves only as a validation case.
record.recipe_differences: It studies mod-p division with a 2-layer transformer and adds DLR and feature-use visualization; it reports selected before- and after-grokking checkpoints rather than testing how the delay varies with training-set size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome differs by training step: step 200 is before grokking and step 3000 is after grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Across grokking on mod-97 division, the last-layer low-rank richness metric DLR drops from 0.51 (step 200) to 0.11 (step 3000).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking coincides with a measurable lazy-to-rich shift in last-layer feature rank, detectable without reference to accuracy.

record.problems: For the grokking result, only two checkpoints are reported in the table, no numerical chance baseline is stated, and training-set size is not varied. Accuracy uncertainties are not reported for these checkpoints.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; quantified delay length. Only two checkpoints are reported.
Circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, and progress measures anticipating the jump.
Grokking on non-algorithmic data; switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm.
All of it. Weight-decay experiments are on CIFAR-10 richness, not grokking.
All of it. Adam is used, but optimizer effects are not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Grokking setup (Fig. 12, Table 9/10): 4,656 training samples, Adam lr 1e-3, betas [0.9, 0.98], no weight decay, 4000 steps. Because the study is T4, no verdicts are given. If curators instead treat the R1–R4 reproduction as a weak replication, it would at most be a minimal 'supports' for V1's train-saturates-before-test pattern, with no evidence on the dataset-size dependence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

It does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, track gradual circuit formation or removal of memorizing components, or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate the accuracy jump.

Image-task experiments report richness and performance under varied training factors, but do not test grokking-like delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or switch such delays through initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
Weight-decay comparisons do not test the proposed efficiency account, a critical dataset size for grokking, or ungrokking below that size.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs or test convergence to the same identifiable algorithm.
The study does not test whether grokking is caused by optimizer or numerical artifacts.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure training accuracy at the before-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: Step 200 is identified as before grokking; the paper reports training accuracy already at 100%.
rows.check: Checkpoint chosen by the authors to mark the 'before grokking' point for metric validation. It is a setup value, not a measurement designed to test V1. No uncertainty is reported for accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure test accuracy at the before-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: The paper identifies this checkpoint as before grokking; it does not state a numerical chance baseline.
rows.check: Selected checkpoint value. Chance for 97 classes is about 1%, so 5.2% is slightly above chance, not exactly chance. The record's 'baseline not stated' is correct. This is a setup value used for metric validation.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure training accuracy at the after-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: Training accuracy remains at 100% at the later checkpoint.
rows.check: Selected checkpoint value used for metric validation, not a test.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure test accuracy at the after-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: The paper identifies this checkpoint as after grokking.
rows.check: Selected checkpoint value used for metric validation. The grokking delay itself (onset step, duration) is never quantified.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure DLR at the before-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: The paper presents DLR as a richness measure, with lower values indicating richer dynamics.
rows.check: DLR is the study's own richness metric, not a measure named by any version. Its value at step 200 is 0.51 ±0.04.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure DLR at the after-grokking checkpoint.
rows.note: The paper says DLR captures the lazy-to-rich transition; the measure is not itself a measure of gradual circuit formation or memorizing-component removal.
rows.check: DLR is the study's own metric. The drop to 0.11 ±0.01 validates the method; it does not test the lazy-to-rich switching described in V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 2-layer transformer on mod-p division (Mod 97), steps 200 and 3000
reader_labels.reason: Training accuracy is 100% at both checkpoints while test accuracy changes from 5.2% before grokking to 99.8% after it (R1–R4).
